articles.title: FMCG’s FII nightmare! $5.2 billion selloff in 12 straight months. Are stocks set for a rebound?
articles.content: Over the past year, foreign investors have unloaded $5.2 billion worth of FMCG stocks, largely due to the challenges stemming from inflated valuations and rising input costs. Companies are now transferring these increased costs to customers, resulting in weak volume growth and declining margins. For a recovery to take shape, analysts emphasize the need for enhanced consumer spending and stable commodity prices.

articles.title: Zydus Lifesciences shares drop 3% after Q1 earnings. Here's why Nuvama upgraded rating, hiked target
articles.content: Shares of Zydus Lifesciences saw a decline of more than two percent following the announcement of a notable profit drop. The net profit plunged thirty-six percent year-on-year for the first quarter, despite a nearly twenty-two percent increase in operational revenue. Expenses surged by over forty-one percent. However, the managing director remains optimistic about future prospects. Analysts at Nuvama have upgraded the stock to 'Buy', setting a higher price target.

articles.title: Missed these IPOs after cold debuts? 11 stocks have since soared up to 222% in few months
articles.content: Despite underwhelming debuts for eleven IPOs, the market has witnessed a remarkable recovery in their valuations. Stocks have soared impressively, with gains ranging from 23% to a staggering 222% over their initial offer prices. Notably, Omnitech Engineering rebounded dramatically, rising by 222% after an initial drop of 9.63%. This underscores the fact that performance on listing day may not accurately predict long-term success.

articles.title: Sensex falls over 200 points, Nifty below 24,450 as oil nears $90/barrel. What lies ahead?
articles.content: On Wednesday, Indian stocks experienced a downturn as oil prices approached $90 per barrel.  Analysts attribute this decline to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which are hampering market momentum. Despite this, the resilience of India's growth suggests improved corporate earnings for FY27, while mid and small-cap stocks have been highly active due to recent results.

articles.title: Godrej Consumer Products shares tank 10% after CEO’s sudden exit; HSBC downgrades to Hold
articles.content: Godrej Consumer Products shares declined 10% following the sudden resignation of CEO Sudhir Sitapati, who announced his work was finished and it was time for new beginnings. HSBC nalysts have since downgraded the stock, highlighting potential uncertainties and execution hurdles ahead, despite the company showcasing strong Q1 performance with impressive profit and revenue growth. Aasif Malbari is set to take charge as the new CEO.

articles.title: Global Market: Kospi extends winning streak as AI optimism lifts chip stocks
articles.content: South Korean shares rose for a third straight session, with the Kospi gaining 3.46% as chipmakers rallied on optimism over strong AI infrastructure demand. Samsung Electronics jumped 6.16% and SK Hynix 3.86%. Foreign investors bought Korean equities worth 899.6 billion won, while broader markets remained mixed and the won weakened slightly.

articles.title: Tata Sons’ IPO can take a page from a Hong Kong titan
articles.content: RBI's requirement for upper-layer shadow lenders leaves Tata Sons facing an inevitable public listing. To resolve long-standing friction with minority owner Shapoorji Pallonji Group over illiquid shares, Tata Sons could emulate Scottish group Jardine Matheson by simplifying its corporate structure, buying out SP Group's stake, and using differential voting rights during an IPO to preserve control and financial stability.
